items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1967-02-09
items.q: I thought it was Buddy DeFranco on clarinet or something like that.

ctx.x: That's who you have to do the study. So the changes, Albert, in the rhythm section have only really come, you think, in the New Orleans men, the change came with the equipment more than with their basic approach. I mean, they got, when they probably moved from New Orleans and there's different sorts of cymbal and things came in, naturally they would introduce those into their kit and that would be another sort of variety of sound to the whole thing.

That's right. Yes. You see, even your musicians, when I left New Orleans, I thought it was that type of music all over the world. And I was disappointed when I heard a lot of great musicians playing dance music, you know. Yes. They were playing without that beat, what you call a beat now, you know. Yes. They were playing with notes, but they weren't swinging. And they didn't have it in them. Now, the music has changed quite a bit and has improved quite a bit. And to prove it, when I first came to Europe, I've…
Do you think the same goes for European rhythm sections? Because I think this is where we tend to fall short of the American.
